title: Diwali Enters State Capitols And City Halls Across Pacific Northwest
excerpt: Five governors hosted first-ever official Diwali celebrations, 22 Washington cities lit lamps in council chambers, and President Trump marked the festival in the Oval Office.
body:
• Governors in Idaho, Nebraska, Montana, North Dakota and Washington hosted Diwali celebrations at state capitols and official residences for the first time, in a programme organised with the Consulate General of India in Seattle.
  • In Washington, 22 cities in the Greater Seattle area held Diwali ceremonies in their city council chambers, in a region the Consulate says is home to nearly 200,000 Indian Americans.
  • President Donald Trump marked Diwali in the Oval Office, where entrepreneur Vishal Gondal presented him with a copy of the Hanuman Chalisa.
  • A sixth state celebration is scheduled in Oregon, at the State Capitol in Salem on November 10, alongside ceremonies in Seattle and King County.

Diwali was celebrated inside state capitols, governors' residences and city halls across the Pacific Northwest this year, as five governors hosted official festivities for the first time and President Donald Trump marked the festival in the Oval Office.

The state programme began in mid-October and was organised with community leaders and co-hosted by the Consulate General of India in Seattle, according to India Weekly. The Consulate described the events as the first governor-hosted Diwali celebrations at the respective capitols and residences.

Five capitols, five firsts

Idaho Governor Brad Little hosted a celebration at the State Capitol Rotunda in Boise on October 16. Nebraska Governor Jim Pillen hosted a ceremony at the Governor's Mansion in Lincoln on October 20. Montana Governor Greg Gianforte welcomed guests to his official residence in Helena on October 26, and North Dakota Governor Kelly Armstrong hosted festivities at the Governor's Residence in Bismarck on October 29, joining First Lady Kjersti Armstrong and the Consul General for the ceremonial lamp-lighting, hi INDiA reported. Washington Governor Bob Ferguson addressed a celebration at the Rotunda of the State Capitol in Olympia on November 4.

"We are proud to be home to one of the largest shares of Indian Americans in the country. And during the previous decade, we had the fastest-growing Indian American population in the entire country."

— Bob Ferguson, Governor of Washington

Pillen encouraged families to preserve their traditions. "It's really important that you keep these traditions alive in your families. Never, ever, ever let the light go out!" he said, according to India Weekly. Armstrong described diversity as a strength and said the relationship extended "at an international level, at a trade level, at a state-to-state level, at a diplomatic level, but most importantly, a human level."

City halls join in

In Washington, 22 cities in the Greater Seattle area held individual Diwali ceremonies inside their city council chambers, with mayors presiding over lamp-lighting ceremonies attended by council members. The cities named in the Consulate's account include Auburn, Everett, Marysville, Kirkland, Bellevue, Tukwila, Medina, Bothell, SeaTac, DuPont, Spokane, Issaquah, Edmonds, Lynnwood, Duvall, Tacoma, Mukilteo and Kent. Further ceremonies are scheduled in Snoqualmie, King County and the City of Seattle on November 10.

Several state and city governments also issued proclamations recognising Diwali as a festival symbolising the triumph of light over darkness, and acknowledging the Indian-American community's contributions. In February 2026, the Washington State Senate passed a bill recognising Diwali and Bandi Chhor Divas as legislatively recognised observances — non-legal holidays, rather than official public holidays, India Weekly reported.

At the White House

In Washington, D.C., Trump participated in a ceremonial diya-lighting in the Oval Office. Indian tech entrepreneur Vishal Gondal, founder of GOQii, presented the president with a copy of the Hanuman Chalisa and shared the moment on X, according to ANI reporting. "A moment of shared light in the Oval Office. Honoured to celebrate Diwali with President Donald Trump and proud to gift him with a copy of the Hanuman Chalisa," Gondal posted. Chef Vikas Khanna and former Canadian parliamentarian Ruby Dhalla were also among those present, ANI reported.

The Pacific Northwest programme concludes on November 10, when Oregon Governor Tina Kotek is scheduled to host a Diwali ceremony at the State Capitol in Salem. For diaspora families in the region, the practical change is recognition in civic space: Diwali is now marked where laws are made and cities are run, not only in temples and homes.
